title: Add Server-Sent Events Support for Streaming Chat Completions
body:
## Summary

Support `stream: true` in `POST /v1/chat/completions` using OpenAI-compatible Server-Sent Events (SSE).

## Why

The current API focuses on completed responses. Clients that expect token-by-token output cannot show a response until generation finishes, which makes long local generations feel unresponsive and limits compatibility with OpenAI SDK integrations.

## Scope

- Return `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and emit incremental `data: {...}\n\n` chunks for streaming requests.
- Send a final `data: [DONE]\n\n` event after successful completion.
- Keep the existing non-streaming response behavior unchanged.
- Propagate client disconnects to the runtime so generation can stop promptly.
- Return clear HTTP errors before streaming begins; document how errors are represented after headers have been sent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An OpenAI-compatible client can consume a streamed response incrementally.
- Chunks contain stable completion IDs, model IDs, and valid delta objects.
- A completed stream ends with `[DONE]`; a disconnected client does not leave generation running unnecessarily.
- Add API tests for streaming success, runtime failure, and client cancellation.
- Document a `curl -N` example.

## References

LM Studio's CLI/API work shows the value of preserving long-lived stream lifecycles and keeping machine-readable output clean (for example, merged PRs [#390](https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lms/pull/390) and [#461](https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lms/pull/461)).

title: Add a Downloaded Model Integrity Check and Repair Flow
body:
## Summary

Add an explicit way to verify downloaded model files and identify incomplete or corrupted downloads before attempting to load them.

## Problem

A file can exist at its expected path even when a download was interrupted or the file was modified outside deepLocal. A later runtime load then fails with a backend error that may not identify the damaged file or suggest a repair.

## Proposed Behavior

- Persist expected file size and, when the source provides one, a checksum or revision identifier with each completed download.
- Add a **Verify** action for a model and show whether it is valid, incomplete, or changed since download.
- Offer a safe re-download action for invalid files. Do not overwrite a valid model without clear user confirmation.
- Show per-file progress and retain enough state to recover after an app restart.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Verification does not load the model into memory.
- Missing, truncated, and mismatched files produce distinct, actionable results.
- The UI identifies which file failed and offers a repair path.
- Cover verification and interrupted repair behavior with storage and UI tests.
- Document the limits when the upstream source provides no checksum.

## References

LM Studio's resolved model-selection and import fixes emphasize preserving exact artifact identity and validating user-visible outcomes (for example, [#417](https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lms/pull/417) and [#438](https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lms/pull/438)).

title: Add a Privacy-Preserving Diagnostics Export
body:
## Summary

Provide a user-initiated diagnostics bundle that helps report installation, runtime, and model-load problems without collecting prompts, document contents, or credentials.

## Proposed Bundle

Include app and crate versions, operating system and architecture, detected CPU/GPU summary, runtime executable path and version, server configuration with secrets removed, recent structured error entries, and relevant health-check results.

## Requirements

- Make export explicit and show a preview of the included categories before writing the file.
- Redact Hugging Face tokens, API keys, authorization headers, prompt text, generated text, document paths where practical, and personal directory names.
- Provide a clear way to exclude logs entirely.
- Write the archive to a user-selected location and do not upload it automatically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Automated tests prove known secret patterns and chat/document content are absent from exported data.
- Export works when the runtime is missing or fails to start.
- The UI explains the bundle contents and destination.
- Add troubleshooting documentation describing how to attach the bundle to a bug report.

## References

Resolved LM Studio reports show that precise runtime and platform context makes issues actionable; PR [#420](https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lms/pull/420) made the selected runtime visible in normal output. This issue applies the same diagnostic principle while keeping local user data private.

title: Add Model Library Health Checks and Re-Link Missing Files
body:
## Summary

Detect when a model tracked by deepLocal has been moved or removed outside the app, and provide a safe way to locate it again.

## Problem

The model library can become stale if a user reorganizes storage, mounts an external drive, or removes a file using the operating system. Showing a broken entry without a recovery action makes it difficult to distinguish a missing model from a runtime failure.

## Proposed Behavior

- Check tracked model paths when opening the Models page and before loading.
- Distinguish **available**, **missing**, **unreachable storage**, and **unsupported file** states.
- Add a **Locate file** action that updates the stored path after validating the selected artifact.
- Preserve model metadata and chat history when the file is re-linked.
- Never delete files as part of a health check.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Missing entries remain visible with a clear recovery action.
- Re-linking preserves the model's identity and related records.
- Offline external volumes do not trigger destructive cleanup or false deletion.
- Add tests for moved files, unavailable volumes, invalid replacements, and successful re-linking.

## References

LM Studio's fixes for import paths and exact variant selection ([#438](https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lms/pull/438), [#417](https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lms/pull/417)) illustrate why model identity and filesystem paths should remain correct through recovery workflows.

title: Add a Reproducible Local Model Benchmark History
body:
## Summary

Let users run a small, repeatable benchmark for an installed model and compare results over time.

## Metrics

Record model identifier and file, runtime/backend and version, load options, hardware summary, time to first token, prompt processing rate, generation tokens per second, and completion timestamp.

## Requirements

- Use a fixed, clearly disclosed local prompt and configurable run count.
- Keep prompt and generated text out of persisted benchmark records.
- Mark results as incomparable when key conditions differ, such as runtime, backend, quantization, or load settings.
- Allow users to delete benchmark history.
- Clearly label results as measurements for the current machine rather than universal model rankings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Users can run the benchmark from a model details view and inspect prior runs.
- Failed and cancelled runs are represented with an actionable status.
- Stored measurements include enough environment metadata to interpret differences.
- Add deterministic tests for metric parsing and history persistence.

## References

LM Studio's hardware survey and load-progress work (for example, [#455](https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lms/pull/455) and [#569](https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lms/pull/569)) show the value of consistent, contextual runtime measurements.

title: Expand OpenAI API Compatibility Tests and Publish a Compatibility Matrix
body:
## Summary

Create a documented compatibility matrix for deepLocal's OpenAI-style API and automate contract tests for the supported request and response shapes.

## Scope

Cover `/v1/models` and `/v1/chat/completions`, including required and optional fields, supported generation parameters, error responses, model identifiers, and streaming once available.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add table-driven tests for valid requests, missing fields, unknown models, invalid parameter ranges, and runtime errors.
- Verify JSON responses contain no human-readable logging or unrelated fields.
- Document supported and unsupported OpenAI SDK behavior with concrete examples.
- Keep compatibility claims specific to tested behavior rather than implying full API parity.

## Why

A small API shape change can break SDK integrations even when the UI continues to work. Explicit contract tests give contributors a quick way to see which behavior is intentional and prevent accidental regressions.

## References

LM Studio merged a focused fix to make `lms server status --json` emit JSON only ([#461](https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lms/pull/461)), illustrating how clean machine-readable contracts improve automation and client compatibility.

title: Improve Model Load Failure Messages with Recovery Guidance
body:
## Summary

Translate common model-load failures into concise explanations that identify the likely cause and give the user a safe next step.

## Examples

- The model file is missing or cannot be read.
- The selected runtime is missing or incompatible with the operating system.
- The model architecture is unsupported by the installed runtime.
- Available memory appears insufficient for the selected load options.
- A requested GPU backend or device is unavailable.

## Requirements

- Preserve the underlying diagnostic details in logs for troubleshooting.
- Do not claim a cause when the runtime cannot determine one; use a neutral message in that case.
- Link each explanation to a relevant action, such as locating the file, choosing another runtime, or reducing context/batch settings.
- Avoid recommending deletion or re-download unless integrity checks support that diagnosis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The UI displays a distinct message for each recognized error category.
- Unknown errors still show a useful fallback and a copyable technical detail.
- Unit tests cover categorization and fallback behavior.
- Add a troubleshooting page mapping common errors to recovery steps.

## References

LM Studio has merged targeted error-message improvements such as [#410](https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lms/pull/410) and Linux prerequisite detection in [#492](https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lms/pull/492). These changes make failures actionable without hiding technical details.

title: Add Keyboard-Only Navigation and Accessibility Checks
body:
## Summary

Make the main desktop workflows usable with a keyboard and screen reader, and add repeatable checks to prevent regressions.

## Workflows

Cover navigation between pages, model search and selection, download controls, model loading, chat composition and send, document management, settings, dialogs, and error recovery.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every interactive control has a visible focus state and an accessible name.
- Dialogs manage focus on open/close and support expected keyboard actions.
- Form errors are associated with their inputs and announced accessibly.
- Chat generation and download status updates are exposed without excessive announcements.
- Add automated accessibility checks to component tests and a keyboard-focused end-to-end smoke test.
- Document any known exceptions with a follow-up issue.

## Why

As the application gains model management, chat, documents, and settings workflows, keyboard access and clear status announcements are core usability requirements rather than isolated UI polish.

## References

LM Studio's accepted chat input improvements, including keyboard shortcuts and pasted-text handling ([#418](https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lms/pull/418), [#451](https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lms/pull/451)), show how careful interaction details benefit CLI users. This issue applies the same attention to desktop accessibility.
